neet_phy_u03_t03_1.working: Momentum is conserved. The bullet's momentum is 0.02 × 400 = 8 kg·m/s. The gun's recoil speed is 8/4 = 2 m/s.

neet_phy_u03_t03_2.working: The fragments have equal and opposite momenta, p = 2 × 30 = 60 kg·m/s. KE of the 3 kg fragment = p²/2m = 3600/6 = 600 J.

neet_phy_u03_t03_3.working: The resultant of two equal momenta of 6 at 120° is √(36 + 36 + 2·36·cos120°) = 6. The third fragment's momentum must cancel this, so its magnitude is 6 kg·m/s.

neet_phy_u03_t03_4.working: A: zero net external force means momentum stays constant (II). B: kinetic energy is not conserved in an inelastic collision (III). C: the fragments' momenta sum to zero (I). D: with only a vertical external force, momentum is conserved horizontally only (IV).

neet_phy_u03_t03_5.working: A is true: internal forces cannot change total momentum. B is true: equal momenta and KE = p²/2m give the lighter piece more KE. C is false: KE is not conserved in inelastic collisions. D is true: equal and antiparallel momenta sum to zero. E is false: recoil speed = mv/M depends on the gun's mass.
